+### Subsequent native recall tool qualification
+
+A later **affected-scope** window used accepted, Entire-pushed source **`d4ba7faacf8af17c1c43d2d6c37bab47f45ba32f`**. The approved read-only recall completed in **28,315.882 ms**, within its original **30,000 ms** deadline, after one exact approval. Its native result and correct apricot answer completed. A separate never-approved write was cancelled in **18,119.743 ms**, with zero tool result, owned tool effects, continuation or assistant output. Both used first attempts only. The earlier deadline failures above remain failures.
+
+The new native recall composition actually ran. Its tool action took **6,862.334 ms**, versus **6,804.213 ms** in the prior window; this does **not** establish an action-speed gain. Within that action, the first active-tool check took 1,100.300 ms, recall preparation 1,313.108 ms, terminal capture 875.752 ms and result attachment 392.151 ms. The embedding itself took 326 ms. These are nested spans, not an additive client latency partition. Protected source/authority checks and separate financial capture/attachment remain required.
+
+The ordinary default-Normal seed answered correctly at **6,260.1 ms** to first painted text, missing its 6,000 ms target. The unchanged CLI/Chat/all-mode matrix was not rerun. Eight startup qualifications, **671 native checks** and **82 stable final readback checks** passed. Target accounting retained **35 unique operations / 35 first attempts / 5,400,000 UNKNOWN units**, with zero active slots or reservations. Cleanup verified **21 fresh absences**, the original launcher joined130, and the owned browser and clients closed.
+
+Official metadata also identifies eight retrying observation transactions among77 observed executions: five conflicted with execution-row writes, two with run-row writes and one with memory-progress writes. The tool action itself had no retrying child. These database retries are distinct from paid model retries and do not explain the whole response interval. The modified goal remains **4/6 milestones (66.7%)**, with cloud timing qualification and final independent audit open.

+# Disposable Cortex sandbox
+
+From **Project-Cortex-Proofs**, with Docker Desktop running:
+
+```sh
+./start-sandbox.sh
+```
+
+Every run creates a **new Docker container and new disposable Convex development database** in the dedicated `cortex-sandboxes` project (team325340/project3200658). Your existing Convex login is required. GitHub access is unnecessary. The launcher uses Node24.15.0/npm12.2.0, the local SDK/CLI/provider0.39.0 candidates, and genuine Basic/Vercel demos1.5.0 from catalog1.4.1. It currently selects the reviewed `manual-sandbox-memory-effort-native-recall-2026-10-15` kit, backed by **Project-Cortex** commit `d4ba7faacf8af17c1c43d2d6c37bab47f45ba32f`, pushed to Entire. Packages are unpublished.
+
+Wait for the printed session ID, container name and demo URL. Open the URL and paste the owner token into **Connect**. The launcher copies that session’s token to the local clipboard without printing it; pass `--no-copy` to preserve your clipboard. Signing and account credentials stay outside Docker.
+
+**Press Ctrl-C in the launcher terminal to clean up both the container and disposable database.** Normal exit, setup failure and SIGTERM also enter owned cleanup. Hard termination or unavailable services can leave cleanup pending; use the exact session ID to recover:
+
+```sh
+./start-sandbox.sh cleanup SESSION_ID
+```
+
+The shared sandbox project and accepted kit remain. There is no global prune or unrelated-project cleanup. Union Arena is outside this workflow.
+
+## Launch options
+
+```sh
+./start-sandbox.sh --help
+./start-sandbox.sh --dry-run
+./start-sandbox.sh --no-copy
+./start-sandbox.sh --smoke
+```
+
+`--dry-run` creates no resources and makes no inference calls. Every normal setup makes **eight real, fixed Gateway qualification calls**, including images, with no automatic paid retry. Their maximum retained UNKNOWN-liability ceiling is **$2.70**, rather than a known charge. Manual requests retain **$3/run, $10/tenant and concurrency2** controls. Video remains deferred because Convex does not support asynchronous Gateway video generation.
+
+## Run the canonical demos
+
+Use the Vercel URL printed at startup. For the Basic CLI, use the printed container name in another terminal:
+
+```sh
+docker exec -it --workdir /work/basic NAME npm start
+docker exec --workdir /work/basic NAME cortex --help
+```
+
+Ordinary Agent **version1** has automatic backend memory and no advertised tools. Explicit tool tests use **version2** of the same published Agent ID. In Vercel, select **Agent version2 → Use agent version**. In Basic:
+
+```sh
+docker exec -it --env AGENT_VERSION=2 --workdir /work/basic NAME npm start
+```
+
+Selecting version2 does not approve a tool. Restart without the override for ordinary version1 chat.
+
+## Manual test scenarios
+
+1. With ordinary version1, send **My favorite fruit is apricot.** Check that the answer appears and asynchronous memory reaches facts/vector readiness. Ordinary approved turns are already retained and indexed; a plain assertion needs no manual memory-tool approval.
+2. Choose **New chat**, then ask **What is my favorite fruit?** Confirm apricot is recalled after indexing. Repeat using each effort selector. A same-conversation answer alone does not prove indexed retrieval.
+3. Select explicit version2 and request **Use memory_recall to retrieve my favorite fruit.** Inspect the pending request and approve it once. Confirm a durable tool result and correct answer; disconnect/reconnect the same run without sending another intent.
+4. Request a separate `memory_remember` tool, cancel before approval, and confirm no approved tool result or tool-owned write. Ordinary indexing of an already approved user input is a separate effect. Test reader write denial and outsider scope denial with the token commands below.
+5. Upload a small private file, compare authenticated downloaded bytes, test outsider denial and reject files above **20,000,000 bytes**.
+6. Explicitly request one image using the qualified **1024×1024, low-quality PNG** contract and inspect its retained private result. Unsupported options should refuse.
+
+Normal is the default. Basic accepts `/effort fast`, `/effort normal`, `/effort high` and `/effort max`.
+
+| Effort | Maximum logical hops | Shared optional-entry ceiling | Hosted first-answer target |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| Fast |2|4|3s|
+| Normal (default) |4|8|6s|
+| High |8|16|8s|
+| Max |No preset|Context-fit|30s|
+
+A direct relevant match is depth1 regardless of age; related evidence adds hops. Joins and authorization reads add none. The entry ceiling is shared across history, memories, facts and pending context. All modes retain work, bytes, deadlines, cost controls and the qualified32,768-unit whole-input bound. The **complete canonical transcript remains stored as individual message rows**. Selection bounds the model request and does not delete history. Max can still report partial coverage.
+
+## Credentials and diagnostics
+
+Tokens last at most one hour and refresh while the launcher runs. Use the printed session UUID:
+
+```sh
+./start-sandbox.sh refresh-tokens SESSION_ID
+./start-sandbox.sh copy-token SESSION_ID owner
+./start-sandbox.sh copy-token SESSION_ID reader
+./start-sandbox.sh copy-token SESSION_ID outsider
+```
+
+Paste a renewed token into **Refresh token**. Keep an uncertain request’s run/request identity instead of automatically retrying it. Private session keys are removed after successful cleanup; redacted receipts remain in `.sandbox-env-runs/SESSION_ID/receipts`.
+
+For client timing, launch with `CORTEX_RUNTIME_LATENCY_TRACE=1 ./start-sandbox.sh`. Backend tracing is enabled separately only on the verified disposable target. Browser paint, CLI stdout, response completion, memory readiness and titles have distinct clocks/boundaries.
+
+## Current qualification and limits
+
+The latest affected window passed eight startup calls,671 native checks,82 final readback checks, approved readonly completion in28.316s within its original30s deadline, and never-approved write cancellation in18.120s with zero approved tool effects. The Normal browser seed was correct at6.260s and missed6s. Tool action6.862s versus prior6.804s establishes no measured action-speed gain. All35 operations used first attempts, retaining5.4M UNKNOWN units with zero slots/reservations. The launcher joined130 and21 fresh absence checks verified cleanup.
+
+The last full browser matrix on unchanged ordinary paths had correct answers at4.895/3.327/3.193/3.628/4.845/4.095s; both Fast samples missed3s. Correct CLI replies at7.789/10.286s and genuine Chat at10.995s missed Normal6s. These are individual samples, not percentiles or guarantees. The modified follow-up remains4/6 milestones (66.7%) pending its latency acceptance rule and final independent audit. Earlier failures stay recorded; no partial source or setup pass certifies full completion.
+
+Historical receipts live in **Project-Cortex** `_goals/convex-backend-runtime-2026-10-02/qa/sandbox-chat-latency-2026-10-12/`. The previous guide is retained below as written; statements about “current” or “next” candidates there are historical. Missing C7 backing/custody and asynchronous video remain unqualified.
